reason: The cited evidence (E1) concerns AlNbTiZr medium-entropy alloy coatings on zirconium alloy, not an ultra-thin Al-rich interlayer beneath a Cr coating. It does not address Cr–Zr interdiffusion, Al2O3 barrier formation at a Cr/Al interface, or performance in high-temperature steam. Therefore, none of the key premises are supported by the cited passage.
premises: An Al-rich interlayer can form a stable, continuous Al2O3 barrier at the Cr/Al interface during high-temperature steam exposure.
This Al2O3 barrier restricts Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
The barrier remains stable and protective under normal subcritical-water conditions (~300–400°C).
The intervention is effective for a Cr coating on a zirconium-alloy substrate.
